subject: Bridge memo: QBR customer triage  Suncrest Analytics
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Bridge memo: QBR customer triage - Suncrest Analytics

Team -

Attached is a concise bridge memo for tomorrow's QBR prep deck for Suncrest Analytics. High-level summary up top; details and suggested asks below. Please read and flag anything you disagree with by EOD.

Executive summary: Suncrest is mid-risk for renewal. Product stability has improved but procurement and legal timelines have slipped. Financially they are healthy (strong NRR potential) but procurement requires an internal approvals package; this is the gating item.

Customer health highlights:
- Usage: steady - 32% q/q growth in token consumption driven by a new recommendation pipeline (attached snapshot).
- Reliability: two P1 incidents in last 90 days (Aug, Oct). Mitigation: runtime patch deployed; customer wants post-mortem on next call.
- Integration: SE worked through L2 caching issue; still seeing 5-7% error spikes on long-run batches.

Renewal risk register (top 6 signals):
1) Procurement delay - buyer says legal needs 3 internal approvals; expected sign date now 2028-01-20 (owner: Jordan).
2) Pricing sensitivity - procurement pushing for additional 18% discount tied to committed volume (owner: Lauren).
3) Technical latency spikes on batch jobs (owner: Monica).
4) Exec attention required - CTO requested ROI summary and brief demo for execs (owner: Soojin).
5) Integration risk - dependency on a third-party inference cache (owner: Monica).
6) Replacement risk - competitive eval scheduled by buyer for Dec 12 (owner: Jordan).

Immediate asks (what I want at EOD today):
- Jordan: confirm updated ARR and proposed discount elasticity (one-line + supporting spreadsheet).
- Lauren: draft a short email for Procurement explaining our proposed approval flow and a targeted signature date.
- Monica: 1-page technical note on the latency spikes with short-term mitigations and ETA for full fix.
- All: flag any Exec-level blockers so I can escalate to Maria or CTO if needed.

Attachments: suncrest-health-snapshot.pdf, MAP_Suncrest_v2.xlsx, procurement-questions-annotated.docx

I will synthesize inputs into a single slide for the QBR.

Thanks -
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Nov 30, 2027 at 11:05 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick update on ARR and procurement timeline:

Adding the technical context:
- Root cause: the latency spikes correlate with a cache invalidation edge-case when concurrent bulk writes occur. SE ran a repro and we have a short-term mitigation (serialized invalidation window) that reduces spikes by ~85% (patch ready for customer testing).
- Full fix ETA: 3 weeks (code + regression + canary); I'll schedule a canary for a subset of their prod traffic next week.
- Post-mortem: drafting an internal post-mortem; will hand over a customer-facing summary for the QBR.

Suggested exec-level ask: a 20-30 minute demo showing stable performance after mitigation and a concise ROI slide showing how the recommender reduces query costs.

I'll attach the one-pager shortly.

-Monica
